thread:
maria: FYI AcmeApp just opened an escalation — p95/p99 spikes since ~2026-03-16T15:20Z on Dedicated pool dp-78 (model rw-infer/gpt-13b). They see p95 ~2.4s (was ~280ms) and p99 ~6.1s. Some attach_timeouts (504) also in the logs.

jordan: Ack, putting this in high priority. Any repro steps from the customer?

maria: Customer says spike occurs during bursty batches (concurrent requests 40-60) after an idle window. They shared an error snippet: "attach_timeout=120s, provision_queue_len=34"

alex: Can you paste a short curl that reproduces? also need pool metrics (attach_latency, warmup_count, pool_active_gpus).

maria: Repro they ran (from customer):
```
curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \ 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 
  -d '{"model":"rw-infer/gpt-13b","input":"<prompt>","max_tokens":512}' &
# they replayed 50 concurrent clients for ~30s
```

maya: Running Prom queries now. Preliminary: attach_timeouts[1h] for dp-78 = 18, provision_queue_length spikes to 40 during bursts. p95 attach latency jumps to 1.8s at spike.

jordan: That smells like cold-GPU warmup + attach fanout. Any recent changes to dp-78? kernel image updates, autoscale policy, or min_capacity changed?\
maria: No config changes from customer side. Internals: dp-78 has min_capacity=2, max=12, scale_up_delay=30s, warmup_policy=on_attach.

alex: Quick mitigations we can try (low-risk):
- temporarily raise min_capacity for dp-78 to 6
- enable prewarm for that pool (pre-pull kernels + pre-start a fraction of GPUs)
- route customer traffic to hosted fallback for short window (model variant rw-infer/gpt-7b)

jordan: I can bump min_capacity and enable prewarm now. Will monitor. @maria please ask customer for a 20-min maintenance window to avoid impacting them further.

maria: pinged customer, they approved 10-min maintenance and asked for rollback plan.

sre-bot: action_log: raised dp-78.min_capacity -> 6 by jordan at 2026-03-16T15:33Z; enabled pool.prewarm=true

maya: Metrics after change: provision_queue_len drops to <5, attach_timeouts stop increasing, p95 returned to ~350-420ms within 2 minutes. p99 down to ~1.1s. Customer confirms much better.

jordan: Thanks. Temporary fix held. Next steps (owner: eng-runtime):
1) Root cause postmortem: check image pull times / registry rate limits and kernel startup (owner alex)
2) Add randomized staggered warmup + backoff to attach path to avoid thundering herd (owner eng-runtime)
3) Consider permanent increase of min_capacity for high-burst customers or per-customer prewarm options (owner product + sales)

alex: Initial logs show a pattern: image_pull_time median increased from 0.9s -> 6.8s during the burst window and Docker pulls queued on the node. Suspect ephemeral image pull + node sd scaling + registry throttling. Will fetch node logs and open infra ticket.

maria: Customer wants ETA for a permanent fix. I'll coordinate with sales/product. For now they want a config knob to opt into prewarm per pool.

jordan: Created internal incident: INC-2026-0427, linked customer, actions and timeline. Also scheduled a follow-up postmortem meeting tomorrow 09:30 PT.

maria: customer: "Thanks, latency is back to normal for now. Please keep us posted." :thumbsup:

alex: TL;DR: root cause likely cold-GPU warmup amplified by image pull latency + pool min_capacity too low for burst. Mitigations applied: bumped min, enabled prewarm, routed fallback option available. Follow-ups: pre-pull images, staggered warmup, and per-customer prewarm config.

maria: closing thread for now, will update after postmortem.
